_readme: SIMULATOR FIXTURES, NOT GAME CONTENT. Synthetic enemies for Tooling/BalanceSim's PvE mode, so the roster can be measured against PvE-shaped fights (one huge enemy, a swarm, a mixed pack). They are not roster beasts, no game code reads this file, and nothing here is a design decision about real encounters. BaseStats are max-level values scaled by the roster growth curve named in GrowthCurveId (as a beast's are); the simulator then calibrates one difficulty multiplier per encounter, level and kit mode, so only the ratios inside a stat line matter. Elements are cycled over a group's units. MoveRange sits inside the roster's own band (beasts move 2-5): BattleTurnExecutor makes a partial approach (a unit that cannot reach range this turn still walks its move toward the target), so no fixture needs board-spanning movement to engage; fights on the Large swarm arena simply take a turn or two to close. Heavy things move 3 (boss, and the wisps, which also have range 3), fast melee hunters 4 (direwolves, and the whole swarm, biters and stingers alike so neither damage category arrives first). The loader requires MoveRange >= 1 and at least one SingleTarget skill. See Tooling/BalanceSim/README.md.

Encounters.Description: One huge enemy: very high HP, heavy single-target hits in both categories every turn, and a periodic area slam. Elementless by default so the boss measures stat lines; use --enemy-element for an elemental variant.

Twenty-four small enemies with low HP and weak melee: half bite (Physical), half sting (Special), so neither defence is favoured. Elements cycle through all ten. Move 4 for every unit: the Large board's zones are 8 apart, so the swarm closes over two turns by partial approach.
Six mid-size enemies: three fast Physical melee hunters in front, three Special casters behind them at range 3. Six different elements.
